## Lisbon Weekend Weather Plan

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cloud-rain.svg

A cool, breezy, and possibly rainy Lisbon weekend calls for a flexible plan with tram/metro use, short neighborhood hops, and indoor backups ready to swap in if showers intensify. This version keeps walking light and clusters sights by area for two adults on a moderate budget.

## 3-Day Lisbon Itinerary with Rain Backups

### Day 1: Fri, 2025-03-28 — Baixa, Chiado, and Riverside Start
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive and check in near Baixa/Chiado or Avenida for easy transit access.
- Afternoon: Start with Praça do Comércio, then take a short ride to Chiado for cafés, bookstores, and covered browsing.
- Indoor backup: Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea or a long lunch in Chiado if rain starts early.
- Dinner: Simple seafood or petiscos near Cais do Sodré; choose a place close to your hotel to avoid a wet return.
- Move smart: Use metro, tram, or short taxi/Uber hops instead of walking long uphill stretches.

Action: [Button: Hotel area map](https://www.google.com/maps/search/Baixa+Chiado+Lisbon+hotels)

### Day 2: Sat, 2025-03-29 — Belém by Transit, Low-Walk Sightseeing
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Go to Belém by tram, train, or rideshare; keep the day compact around a few nearby stops.
- Afternoon: Visit Jerónimos Monastery exterior, then choose one indoor museum: MAAT, Museu Nacional dos Coches, or the Berardo Collection if open.
- Outdoor backup: Riverside promenade only if the weather breaks; otherwise stay with museum-heavy routing.
- Food: Pastéis de Belém plus a casual lunch nearby keeps this day budget-friendly.
- Rain plan: If showers are heavy, skip the promenade and do museum + café + pastry stop only.

Action: [Button: Belém transit plan](https://www.google.com/maps/search/Belem+Lisbon+public+transport)

### Day 3: Sun, 2025-03-30 — Alfama Views, Tram, and Cozy End to the Trip
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: If dry, take Tram 28 or a short taxi to the Alfama edge and do a limited scenic loop with only a few viewpoints.
- Afternoon: Choose one indoor fallback: Lisbon Cathedral area, Fado museum, or a relaxed café/market stop if the rain continues.
- Outdoor backup: Miradouros only for brief photo stops between showers; avoid a full hill walk in wet weather.
- Dinner: End with a relaxed neighborhood meal near your lodging so you can pack and rest without extra travel.
- Move smart: Use tram plus short descents; avoid planning both Alfama and Bairro Alto on foot in one wet afternoon.

Action: [Button: Tram 28 route](https://www.google.com/maps/search/Tram+28+Lisbon+route)

## Rain-Friendly Budget Tips for Two Adults

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/currency-euro.svg
- Stay central: Baixa, Chiado, or Avenida usually cuts transport costs and reduces wet walking.
- Use transit passes or single rides: Best value if you are doing a few clustered hops each day.
- Prioritize 1 paid indoor attraction per day: Mix free viewpoints, church exteriors, and cafés with one museum or monument interior.
- Eat strategically: Breakfast near the hotel, pastry/lunch in the sightseeing area, and one relaxed dinner close by.
- Keep a rideshare fallback: Helpful for steep hills or sudden downpours.

## What to Pack for Cool, Breezy, Rainy Lisbon

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg
- Light waterproof jacket or compact umbrella
- Layered tops: T-shirt or base layer plus sweater or light fleece
- Comfortable water-resistant shoes with grip
- Quick-dry socks and a small day bag cover
- One slightly warmer layer for evenings near the river
- Optional: foldable rain pants if you expect heavier showers

## Quick Actions
